title: Diagnostic code registry -- the one home of what every refusal code MEANS
description: Every refusal the kit can state carries a stable code, and this registry is the only place a code's meaning is declared (ADR-005). The class that raises a refusal names its code; the message, any future `--explain`, any SARIF export and every test are projections of the row. The registry is APPEND-ONLY: a code is issued once, never deleted, never reused and never re-meant. A code that stops being raised is RETIRED -- its row stays, marked, with the version and the reason -- because an outside consumer may still be matching on it, and a deleted row is how a published code gets silently handed to a second meaning. `issued` is the high-water mark: codes are dense from 1 to `issued`, so a deleted row is a gap a gate can see without any history.

prefix.description: The namespace every code carries. Constant for the life of the registry: changing it re-numbers every published code at once.

issued.description: The highest code ever issued. Only ever grows. A new code is `issued + 1`, and this field moves with it in the same change.

code.description: Opaque and sequential. The digits carry NO class: severity is the exit code's job, and a family digit would lie the day a refusal moved between families.

status.description: active: raised today by exactly one refusal class. retired: raised by nothing, kept forever, never reissued.

title.description: One line: the situation this code names, in the host's terms rather than the interpreter's.

explanation.description: What the situation is, why the kit refuses it rather than guessing, and what the operator does next. The text `--explain` would print.

retired.description: Present exactly when status is retired: the kit version the code stopped being raised in, and why.
